questions.q: What is a SQL Server Agent performance condition alert tied to, per this lesson?
options: A specific PerfMon-style counter (object, counter, optional instance) crossing a defined threshold
The size of the transaction log only
The number of users currently logged in
A fixed schedule with no actual condition attached
questions.explain: Performance condition alerts (sp_add_alert) are defined against an object/counter combination, such as Buffer Manager's Page life expectancy, with a comparison and value.

questions.q: What is the main limitation of a fixed-threshold alert like "Page Life Expectancy falls below 300" applied the same way everywhere?
options: The same absolute number can be a real problem on one server and completely normal on another, depending on that server's own buffer pool and workload
Fixed-threshold alerts are not supported by SQL Server Agent at all
Page Life Expectancy cannot be monitored with Agent alerts
Fixed thresholds only work on Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: A single round-number threshold ignores that 'normal' varies by server and workload — the same value can mean very different things on different systems.

questions.q: How does a baseline-comparison alerting job (built on the previous lesson's history table) improve on a fixed threshold?
options: It compares the current reading against that specific server's own stored historical pattern and alerts only on a meaningful deviation from it
It ignores all DMV data and relies purely on guesswork
It removes the need for any operator or notification
It only works during business hours
questions.explain: Comparing against your own baseline history (from the previous lesson) produces a threshold tailored to that server's actual normal range, rather than a generic guessed number.

questions.q: What does an 'operator' refer to in the context of SQL Server Agent alerts?
options: A named notification recipient, created with sp_add_operator, typically notified via Database Mail
A T-SQL arithmetic symbol like + or -
A type of execution plan operator such as a Hash Match
A SQL Server login with sysadmin rights
questions.explain: An operator is the notification target defined for Agent alerts and jobs — the person or distribution list that actually receives the alert.

questions.q: What does this lesson mean by 'alert fatigue,' and why does it matter?
options: A threshold set too sensitively causes so many alerts that real ones get ignored — so sensitivity needs to reflect real variance, not an arbitrary number
SQL Server automatically disables alerts after 24 hours
Operators become physically tired from receiving Database Mail
It refers to a hardware failure in the alerting subsystem
questions.explain: An alert tuned too tightly fires constantly on normal noise, training people to ignore it — exactly the outcome baseline-informed thresholds are meant to avoid.
